newsitem.title: UK: Major aide denies he ruled out UK in EMU 1st wave.
newsitem.headline: Major aide denies he ruled out UK in EMU 1st wave.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major has not ruled out Britain signing up for a single European currency launch on January 1, 1999, a spokesman at his Downing Street office said on Monday.

He said that in an interview with the French newspaper Le Figaro, Major merely said that if the new Euro was launched without "reliable and sustainable convergence" of the economies of participating countries, Britain would not join in.
The spokesman said the interview was conducted by Le Figaro submitting questions to which Major gave written answers in English.
He quoted the relevant answer as being: "If the EU is heading for a single currency without reliable and sustainable convergence, we do not think it would be sensible to go ahead.
"If it did go ahead on this basis, we would certainly not be part of it." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
